description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the “Ratio” (x-axis) and “minADE₂₀ (←)” (y-axis) for five different trajectory prediction methods: TrajICL, Head Tuning, FT, LoRA 16, and LoRA 64. The x-axis, labeled “Ratio,” spans from 0 to 1.0 in linear increments of 0.2, representing the proportion of training data or model capacity used. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←),” ranges from approximately 0.55 to 0.78, indicating the minimum Average Displacement Error over 20 predictions, with lower values signifying better performance. The “Head Tuning” method (orange line with circle markers) starts at the highest performance (~0.78 at Ratio=0.1) and steadily declines to ~0.68 at Ratio=1.0. “LoRA 64” (purple line with diamond markers) begins at ~0.74, drops sharply to ~0.64 at Ratio=0.6, then levels off near 0.61 at Ratio=1.0. “LoRA 16” (red line with square markers) follows a similar downward trend, starting at ~0.74 and ending at ~0.60. “FT” (green line with circle markers) starts at ~0.68, drops steeply to ~0.57 at Ratio=0.7, and remains flat near 0.56 at Ratio=1.0. “TrajICL” (blue line with circle markers) remains relatively stable across all ratios, fluctuating slightly between ~0.60 and 0.61, showing minimal sensitivity to the ratio parameter. All lines are solid, and the legend is positioned in the upper right corner.
